summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and Orbit Integrations to scope a partner integration for GPU-backed inference and potential managed Dedicated/Private deployments. Covered Orbit's typical workloads (real-time multimodal inference, customer-facing chatbots), security/compliance constraints, pilot goals, and next steps around benchmarks and security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-31 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes | Attendees: Samira, Devon, Priya (Redwood)  Ethan, Laura, Miguel (Orbit)

[00:00] Samira Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick round robin, then we can jump in  Devon will cover the tech bits.
[00:18] Ethan Morales: Hi uh Ethan here, CTO at Orbit. Thanks for making time.
[00:22] Laura Chen: Laura, Head of Cloud. Excited to talk GPU options and how we might partner.
[00:30] Devon Lee: Hey team, Devon (SE)  I'll walk through integration patterns and perf expectations.

[01:05] Samira Khan: High level, we're thinking Partner intro / discovery  Orbit builds SaaS integrations for retail customers, you run inference workloads for personalized search and store assistants?
[01:20] Ethan Morales: Yeah that's right. We have a few customers hitting 200-300 qps for embeddings generation and low-latency chat features for storefront agents. Mostly a mix of text and some image features for product attributes.
[01:35] Priya Raman: Got it. When you say 200-300 qps, is that sustained or burst?
[01:42] Ethan Morales: It's bursty. Peak windows during promotions are big  say 10-15 minute bursts. Average steady is more like 30-50 qps.

[02:10] Laura Chen: Important bit for us: data residency and encryption. Some of our retail customers require EU residency and strict KMS integration.
[02:22] Samira Khan: Totally, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC deployments; Dedicated pools can be region pinned. We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
[02:35] Miguel Alvarez: On the infra side, we're curious about latency SLOs. For chat we need sub-200ms token latencies on average. Is that realistic with your runtime?
[02:48] Devon Lee: Short answer: yes for many models when configured right  continuous batching, KV cache, and kernel selection helps. Longer answer: depends on model family, sequence length, and whether you're on hosted vs Dedicated or Private. For example, on Dedicated with A100-equivalent instances we often hit 80-120ms p50 for standard chat flows.

[03:25] Ethan Morales: Cool. Any gotchas around quantization? We've looked at 4-bit quantized weights to save cost.
[03:33] Devon Lee: We support quantization-friendly execution paths. There are tradeoffs  some workloads show slight quality regression. Redwood Optimize gives quantization recommendations per workload; we'll run evals on your prompt set.

[04:10] Laura Chen: Security review question  audit logs and SSO. We integrate with Okta and need detailed request-level audit logging for our customers.
[04:20] Priya Raman: We do SSO/SAML and RBAC; our Console exposes per-route dashboards and tracing hooks. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via forwarders. We'll include sample log formats in the security pack.

[05:00] Miguel Alvarez: Network topology for Private  do you support air-gapped on-prem? We've got a few regulated customers and one potentially wants on-prem where data never leaves the network.
[05:12] Devon Lee: Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem packages with a private control plane option. There's some work on sizing and packaging but we've done a few air-gapped installs. We'll need to plan for kernel compat and driver versions.

[06:00] Ethan Morales: Regarding partner integration, do you have an SDK or connector pattern we should follow?
[06:06] Samira Khan: We have SDKs and a partner integration guide. Typical partner flow: initial discovery -> pilot (benchmarks + handful of customers) -> validated performance -> go-to-market bundle. For SI/SaaS partners we provide reference connectors and co-marketing assets.

[07:00] Devon Lee: Technical note  if you want to run hybrid routing (hosted for low-volume, dedicated for heavy), our smart routing can failover based on capacity and cost. You can pin routes to Dedicated pools.

[07:45] Laura Chen: Pricing model: curious about committed reserved capacity vs usage-based. Our finance folks prefer predictable spend for pilots.
[07:55] Samira Khan: We offer reserved capacity (Dedicated) with monthly or annual commits; there's also usage-based for hosted. For pilots we can do short term reserved windows or mixed approach. I'll share pricing scenarios.

[09:10] Ethan Morales: On benchmarking  what do you need from us?
[09:20] Devon Lee: A representative workload: sample prompts, sequence length distributions, target latency/throughput, and a small validation set for quality checks. We'll run tests across model variants and quantization profiles.

[10:05] Miguel Alvarez: We use Kubernetes in our infra. Any recommendations or compat notes?
[10:12] Priya Raman: For Private on k8s, we recommend particular nv driver versions and CRDs for GPU scheduling; we'll share an ops checklist. There can be subtle issues with kernel drivers on certain cloud images, we've seen that with some 4.x drivers.

[11:00] Ethan Morales: Competitors  we've looked at Lambda Labs and Paperspace for self-host, and also considering Vertex AI for managed endpoints. How does Redwood differentiate?
[11:12] Samira Khan: Redwood focuses on production-inference economics and unified tooling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. We provide rollout controls, per-route dashboards, and Optimize recommendations tailored to your workload. Also emphasis on reliability and built-in fallbacks.

[12:05] Laura Chen: Quick question on model catalog  do you host open models only or do you also support customer-provided models?
[12:12] Devon Lee: Both. We have a curated catalog of open models and also support bringing your own model artifacts; for BYOM we'll help with compilation and kernel selection.

[13:00] Ethan Morales: For pilot scope, can we start with embeddings and a small chat model? Embeddings are big cost center.
[13:10] Samira Khan: Yes, common approach. Start with embeddings benchmarking (cost per 1k tokens) and one chat flow for end-to-end latency and quality.

[14:20] Laura Chen: About logs and PII  some customers require PII redaction. Do you support redaction or preprocessing hooks?
[14:30] Priya Raman: We provide pre-request hooks and can implement on-the-fly redaction or prefix stripping. For Private deployments you can keep full control. We'll note options in the security pack.

[16:00] Miguel Alvarez: Any limitation on model size or GPU types? Some of our customers want Llama 70B style models.
[16:10] Devon Lee: We support large model families; for very large models there are memory and latency tradeoffs. We can recommend sharding/quantization and instance types  A100/H100 classes or multi-GPU sharded setups. We'll map your ROI targets to a config.

[18:00] Ethan Morales: Ok, sounds promising. Let's recap next steps.
[18:10] Samira Khan: Recap: Samira to share partner deck + pricing; Devon to design benchmark plan; Laura to provide sample workloads; Miguel to give staging access. We'll schedule technical deep-dive week of April 12.
[18:28] Laura Chen: That works. Also please include SOC2 docs and sample audit logs when you send the deck.
[18:35] Priya Raman: Will do.

[19:00] Devon Lee: One last note  can we get an initial run at embeddings cost estimate? If you send sample counts per month we can give a ballpark.
[19:10] Ethan Morales: I'll pull numbers and send by Friday.

[19:45] Samira Khan: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep dive.

[20:00] Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript contains some ASR artifacts; product names sometimes mis-transcribed (Redwood Dedicated/Private/Console). References: partner deck link (sent after), security pack (SOC2, ISO sample), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared).
